title: Toward C:open-ended: with a 3-component heritable trait, the kind-specific waste fed vortices populate 33/33 trait classes (held by >= 3 vortices at once) by t=6000 against 12/16 in the kind-blind twin, rising roughly linearly to t~4500 where the 1-component trait had levelled off at 10-12; the count slows after t~4500 (31 -> 33)
summary: world.py: the kind-specific-waste fed vortices (20261027T1245-c58-vortex-waste-novelty) with a trait vector of 3 components carried as 3 trait masses copied linearly where the vortex eats; mutation shifts the whole vortex's trait by 0.4 along a random direction (3 normal draws, normalised; never reads the trait); the waste carries 3 waste-trait masses and G = exp(-|theta - theta_W|^2/(2 0.4^2)). trait3.py (labkit segmentation and tracker, class = tuple round(theta_i/0.4)), seeds 1-2, T=6000: kind-specific waste: classes ever held by >= 3 vortices at t=1500/3000/4500/6000 9/21/31/33 and 7/19/29/33; kind-blind twin 6/10/12/12 and 10/12/14/16 (novelty_1d_vs_3d.png); distinct dominant classes 5/9 vs 3/2; returns to an earlier dominant class 1/3 vs 5/1; daughters within 0.2 of the parent's trait 111/128 and 131/172 (twin 224/259, 193/220); trait jumps of living vortices away from a mutation 0 in all four runs; max generation 20/24 vs 25/25.

finding.operator: kind-specific waste on a 3-component heritable trait (more trait dimensions for the escape from one's own waste)
finding.control: kind-blind waste twin (sw 0: same ecology and mutation draws, gain independent of the trait), seeds 1 2; the 1-component world 20261027T1245-c58-vortex-waste-novelty
finding.result: classes ever held by >= 3 vortices at t=6000: 33/33 vs 12/16 (1-component: 12/10 vs 6/5); growth ~linear to t~4500, then +2/+4 in the last 1500 t

limits: Two seeds, T=6000, 128^2, one parameter point, no dt/2 or grid test, no labkit pack of this world. The negative frequency dependence is written (the waste records the eater's trait and the gain reads it), so escape into new trait cells is expected from the rule; the twin shows the vortices' heredity and the rule, not drift alone, give the excess. The count of classes held by >= 3 grows also in the twin (a 3-D random walk keeps reaching new cells), and in the selective arm it slows after t~4500, so non-saturation is not shown; a T=10000 run on fresh seed 3 is running. Classes are fixed 0.4 bins; 'new' is a bin never held before, not a new phenotype: every trait value has the same intrinsic fitness, so the novelty is in labels that matter only relative to the waste. Heredity is weaker than in the twin (76-87% vs 86-88% of daughters keep the class; within-vortex spread 0.03-0.04 vs 0.015) because diverse traits fuse.
